speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me identify the cause, have you noticed if the rash appeared any specific time after starting a new medication, or if it seems to worsen with heat or sweating?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The clinical picture of a 11-year-old girl with recent prodromal symptoms (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, culminating in a facial rash that spares the perioral area, is classic for this condition. The rash description matches the characteristic "slapped cheek" appearance, and the timing aligns with the typical progression of the illness. No further testing is required at this stage.
